And in my submission, again, the Prosecutor ought to be called upon in the circumstances now of recovering this and perhaps recovering it in a more specific way with this witness. What's the basis of this questioning? If not to establish the very thing that has been renounced by Mr. Re on a previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, frankly speaking, we are not quite familiar with the theory of the Prosecution at this moment, and I believe the testimony of this witness is just to give us some general ideas of the commanders, you know. And whether, you know, the deputy commander has the authority to issue any orders, which is quite normal in the proceedings. And then we also believe that up to now we cannot see that this piece of evidence is relevant to this case at this moment. And -- and since it's a general question, and since it's not directly pointing the fingers to your client, we'll allow this practice to go on. And we'll see, you know, where the Prosecution stands in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Before I come to this document, I would first like to ask you: Do you know the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What's his name? What's his name?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: His name is General Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what was his position in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: He was the chief of the Main Staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. At that time -- at the beginning of the war, he -- there was the post of the commander and then there was the post of the commander of the Main Staff. So he became the Chief of Staff and then also deputy. But this is sort of playing on words now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Was he one of the three deputy commanders when you saw that document earlier on where you were -- he was made -- he was given that rank at that time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: All right. Now, this document I want to show you --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Ms. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you look at this document, please, and tell us what -- what it is.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the commander of the Main Staff of --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Their Honours don't have it in front of them at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours, can you just confirm. If you'd just wait until it comes up in Sanction, please. On the ELMO, Your Honour. Sorry. I don't know which technology we're using when.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: All right. Sorry, Mr. Gusic, I interrupted you. Would you please carry on.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the commander of the Main Staff of the BH Armed Forces. It's from General Rasim Delic on the formation of a professional team in order to coordinate affairs and tasks in the areas of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps. The team's assignments are mentioned, the composition of the team, under 3, the authority of the chief of the Main Staff is mentioned. He is authorised to deal with the problems in the field, and it is also his duty to inform the commander. And if there are exceptional changes, he should consult him before taking certain measures. The task is to commence on the 31st of August. The time by which the task should be carried out is not specified. And at the end it states that a report should be submitted in the course of this mission. Item 3 provides authority to deal with problems, and it's only the Chief of Staff who has such authority. The other members of this team don't have such authority. Only he has the authority to deal with problems in the areas of responsibility mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What authority did Mr. Sefer Halilovic, the accused in this case, have and according to this order and in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: To deal with all problems by issuing orders, if these problems didn't have a radical effect on the organisation and structure of the units where he was carrying out an inspection. So this means that he could issue any kind of orders that concerned the life and work of units. He could issue orders to take certain steps that had to do with arranging combat positions, to initiate certain combat operations. And if more radical measures had to be taken, if it was necessary to take measures which were not usual, in such cases he had to submit a proposal to the commander, and it was only then that he could issue the relevant orders. Radical measures would be measures that have to be taken in a way that changes the situation within a unit. But in the zone of responsibility of a unit, I think that all the orders issued were orders that regulated the life and work of units in the areas of responsibility mentioned, and this is authority confirmed by the supreme military body in these areas, in the areas of responsibility of the 4th and 6th Corps. And as I said, radical measures involve measures which have an effect on the situation in the unit itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So this would be an authority to the Chief of Staff to issue orders, this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's been no objection to leading up to now, but it's the witness's testimony and not those propositions from the Prosecutor that should be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So I'd object to that leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may rephrase your question, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought I was simply repeating what the witness had said, but I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So what authority did the accused have by this order, with respect to orders?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: He could issue orders. He could draft orders that he would sign himself. He could issue orders that had to do with the life and work of units, provided that these orders did not affect the actual situation within the unit itself, provided it didn't change it radically. He could also issue other orders because he wasn't duty-bound to explain to any superior commanders whether measures were radical or not. I or General Pasalic couldn't know whether General Halilovic had consulted the commander. So he could have issued any kind of order. He could have issued a radical order too, and this order would have had to be executed. But according to the line followed when reporting, we would have informed him and the commander that we had received such an order and had carried it out. Regular reports were provided at the end of every day to the Supreme Command Staff, and the commander was informed of such reports. So if any radical orders had been issued, the commander would have been aware of the fact. He would have found out about it within one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. So these orders, would they be binding on every -- all the other units?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Binding? Binding orders. But without this document, the Chief of Staff could issue binding orders, and we received binding orders from General Halilovic without this authorisation, so there were such orders too. Because he wasn't duty-bound to show me his authorisation. If he'd been in Sarajevo and drafted an order, well, that was a binding order for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: And he probably wouldn't have acted in this way if he had not been authorised by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That was the question I was going to ask; who authorised him. And you've just answered it. Now, Mr. Gusic, I would like to take you to the events in Grabovica. Did you ever attend a meeting in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you remember what date this was?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 21st and 22nd of August, as far as I can recall. I think it was the 21st. I may be wrong, but it was certainly the second half of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And who was present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This meeting was attended by commander -- the commander, General Delic; the chief, General Halilovic; the heads of the administrations, General Suljevic, General Bilajac, General Vranj; General Zorlak.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can you summarise --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The corps commanders all except for the commander of the 5th Corps. There was the Air Force commander. I may have omitted to mention someone, but I think that's it for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Other than Sefer Halilovic, were there two other deputy commanders there, the other two deputy commanders of the -- the army?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I would take you now to this document, Mr. Gusic, 01831684, MFI109.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May we refer to Sanction, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now that it's up on Sanction, before I ask you to refer to it, I would like to ask you: What were the general nature of the discussions at the Zenica meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This was the first meeting at which all the commanders had gathered except for the commander of the 5th Corps. So this was the first meeting of corps commanders; however, the commander of the 5th Corps was prevented from coming, as was the commander of Gorazde and the commander of Srebrenica. Those three commanders could not attend the meeting for good reason. In the first part of that meeting, an analysis was carried out of the situation in the areas of responsibility of the various corps. There was discussion of the need to plan new combat operations, the implementation of measures to preserve what had already been achieved, and some general guidelines were issued as to what should be planned in the forthcoming period and what kind of combat operations should be carried out. Some decisions were made about the organisation of the units. There were some doctrinal issues that were debated about the organisation and structure of the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And finally, the meeting ended with the commander setting out his conclusions, and the document I have before me is a document that arrived after this meeting was held. It arrived in the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And, of course, at the front of the document, you have those who were present at the meeting, in which you are listed, and we have the commander, Rasim Delic; the accused, Sefer Halilovic. So are these the attendees that you remember?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Then there are conclusions. These are not the minutes of the Zenica meeting, are they?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Then, number 10, on page 4 of my English version.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Where it says "Tasks"? Under the heading "Tasks"?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. So this is the forthcoming combat actions you were just talking about.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And lower down, you as a commander of the 6th Corps were sent to -- to ask for the necessary organisation and mobilisation for the functioning of the corps. Was the name "Operation Neretva" ever raised at this particular meeting, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But was it discussed there were going to be operations -- combat operations in the Neretva Valley?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honour, there should be no leading on these matters. In any event, there is a transcript of this, and if the witness needs to have his memory refreshed as to what the discussion was, he can. But the objection now is confined to no leading and no putting of propositions to the witness like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Where were these combat activities supposed to take place?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The 6th Corps was given three axes along which it was supposed to plan carry out combat actions. You can see that in paragraph 10. The second item, "Operative Group East" from the 3rd Corps is reassigned to the 6th Corps, the boundary between the 3rd and the 6th Corps being -- this is the axis towards Prozor. The second one is between the 1st and the 6th Corps -- or rather, the areas where their boundary line is between the corps. This is the area in the direction of Kiseljak, that is, Sarajevo. And the third area is in the direction of the 4th Corps, that is, the town of Mostar and the valley of the River Neretva. And pursuant to this, the corps command planned certain activities and the corps command actively worked on this second task, which is to stabilise the lines at Igman and to organise combat operations in the direction of Kiseljak, which is why the forward command post in Fojnica was set up, which I mentioned before. This was the forward command post of the 6th Corps, and Dzevad Tirak, my Chief of Staff, was its commander. The other activities were carried out on the Neretva and Prozor axes, and these activities were conducted by the forward command post of the staff of the Supreme Command headed by General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: When did you --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is not a plan of the operation. This is not even a preparatory order in form. This is simply an indication that something should be planned along these axes, and specific plans had to be worked out afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's -- that's very clear. Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Did you ever hear of Operation Neretva as a military operation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Later, after everything had happened, that's when I heard about it. But in the preparation phase and in the initial stages of implementing the operation, I hadn't heard about it. I heard about it for the first time when the operation was already underway. I'm referring to the name of the operation. I knew that there were preparations, that forces were being brought into the area. I knew the axis along which they would go. And I knew most of the forces that would be activated there. I knew who was in charge of the combat activities. But I did not have access to the plans. I did not know who approved them or how they had been approved.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What else did you know how this plan was to be conducted?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The plan was to be conducted in two directions. There were the two areas between the corps. One was to be in the Neretva River Valley, and the other one was to be in the direction of the town of Prozor. If you analyse the terrain, those are two very important axes which would enable the army forces to join up, to link up -- to link up with the city of Sarajevo, and they would solve all the problems faced by the command of the 4th Corps linking up to the corps of the army, and then toward Prozor we would take the dominant features that would protect our flanks and provide far greater security for life and work along the upper part of the Neretva River. I was present at several meetings where there was discussion of this. The main axis, General Halilovic said to start with that it would be in the Neretva River Valley. However, we had a meeting in Dugo Polje where he changed his decision, and he said the main axis would be in the direction of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can I stop you there, Mr. Gusic, because we will come to these meetings a little later on. I just want to keep the -- the Grabovica incidents at this time. Can I go back and ask you: When were you informed of this operation, if you ever were?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The first information that the operation was going on was in early September, the 2nd or the 3rd of September, when the units left Sarajevo. Because General Halilovic had issued an order that the units should leave Sarajevo, go to Bradina, and be conducted towards Jablanica, and that was the first information we had that an operation was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And who informed you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I received an order from General Halilovic that I was to receive the units at Bradina. I wasn't informed. I was given the order to receive the units at Bradina, because General Halilovic was not duty-bound to inform me about his activities. According to the chain of command, he had to inform only the commander of the armed forces, Rasim Delic. He was not duty-bound to inform me of what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Which units are you referring to, Mr. Gusic, that you had to receive?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: These were the units of the 9th and 10th Brigade, the Delta Brigade, and another unit -- there were four units. I can't recall all of their names. I can't recall. It escapes me now. But I think there is a document. I think there is an order where you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you asked to take part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. No. The units were asked and I was asked to attend some meetings evaluating the forces, but I was never given any specific tasks in connection with Neretva. I was not in charge of any axis or area of responsibility, nor was I commanding any units participating in these combat activities. I was not given any other tasks except putting some of my units at their disposal, preparing some units, and giving them to -- making them be at the disposal of the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I will now show you a document, 02196110, MFI110.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can we go to Sanction, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you look at this, Mr. Gusic, and tell the -- Your Honours what -- what it is.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is a report. This document did not look like this in its original form. The format would be slightly different. This is the electronic format which was obtained in the communications centre of the Supreme Command, and such documents start with the indication of the communications centre receiving them, the file -- the computer -- the name of the computer file, then in the right-hand corner the person who received them, and then in the left-hand corner the date and time of receipt, and then they would follow the content of the document which I sent to General Halilovic. This is a report. It's about implementing a task. I can't recall precisely what task this refers to. It was probably providing some kind of support, because in the second sentence I mention Dr. Cibo, that's is Safet Cibo, he was the president of the municipalities of Konjic, Jablanica, and Prozor. And he was a representative of the authorities who provided logistic support to the units of the army. He would provide certain foodstuffs, fuel, medicines, and other necessities having to do with the life and work of the units. This probably refers to fuel, and probably the tasks had to do with some kind of transport because I had been unable to contact Dr. Cibo. He was the mayor of three municipalities, so he might have been away.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, we'll take a lot of time if you explain each document in that kind of detail. What I really would like you to say is when you say in this document you're not in a position to accomplish the assignment, could you just explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Very well. It means that the task was closely connected to the support I was supposed to get from Dr. Cibo as the mayor of the municipality. As he had not given me those means, I had to follow the procedure and say that I could not perform this task so that other measures could be taken. I wished to inform General Halilovic that it was not possible to carry out an activity that he had ordered for reasons which I feel are objective.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this Operation Neretva, I would like now to go back to that and ask you where was it to be coordinated and conducted from; did you know?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The operation was coordinated and carried out from the Jablanica forward command post, and General Halilovic was in charge of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Who else was -- you said General Halilovic was in charge. What other members were part of this IKM? Was it called IKM, this forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry for leading that, Your Honour. It's just -- it's the Bosnian acronym for the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact date I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Gusic. I asked you who were the other members.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The members of the command post: There was General Bilajac, Brigadier Vehbija Karic, General Zicro Suljevic, the security organ Namik Dzanko, I think, then it was secured. The command post was in the administrative building of the Jablanica hydroelectric plant, and it was secured by the special purpose unit called Zulfikar. It had its communications centre. I visited this forward command post once or twice. I'm certain that I visited it at least once while it was being set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can we go slowly, please. Where exactly was it located again? Could you please tell the -- Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The command post was in the administrative building of the Jablanica hydroelectric power plant. These were offices in which the forward command post was situated. This was within the compound of the hydroelectric power plant, which could be secured with a small number of troops. It had its telephone line, its communications centre. First they used the communications centre of the 44th Brigade. Later on he had his own communications centre. And I feel that the officers who were at the forward command post with General Halilovic at the time were and still are some of the most professional that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had. General Bilajac, General Suljevic, Brigadier Karic, and certainly General Halilovic. I think that this was a command post that was competent and able to lead the forces on the ground. It was a team with military authority and every other kind of authority with all of us. They were experienced senior soldiers who had been soldiers for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And were these experienced soldiers that you -- the members of the inspection team you've just told us about, were they in your area of responsibility? Did you ever see them there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The members of the team - General Bilajac, General Zicro Suljevic, and the late General Kemo Karisik - frequently came to my area of responsibility very often, quite apart from this task of theirs. And during this assignment, they would frequently come to the command post in Konjic, especially Generals Bilajac and Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, you said that Sefer Halilovic was the commander at the IKM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could he in that capacity issue binding orders, the IKM, to you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you -- would you carry out all orders given to you by the IKM under that -- the command of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Was there ever a time you would refuse to carry out his orders?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I want to very quickly, so I do not waste too much of the Court's time, show five documents, Your Honours, and I will just give you all the names so that they can come up one after the other, which is 00554674, MFI111; 02196114, MFI112; 00577879, MFI113; 02196115, MFI114; 00577876, MFI115.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, might I just request that the P numbers of those be provided if it's been done in paper copy. That would assist us.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that at this moment we also don't have that number yet, but for the later submissions we'll ask the -- the party who adduce any document to get in touch with the registrar or court deputy of this case beforehand so that they could put a so-called MFI number on it. That will greatly facilitate our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I just -- frankly my ears were slow then. I'm trying to accustom to the e-court, and I wasn't taking note of the ERN numbers as they came there. So I wonder if the Prosecutor would be good enough to identify for me now which are the P numbers on the list provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Before they go to the witness so that I can see if I have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's just what we want too.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Apologies to the Defence. I do have the exhibit numbers here. That would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That will be much easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We will refer to them as 65 ter numbers. 41, 48, 75, 79, 81. Now -- may I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, when you see these documents, I want you to be fairly rapid about this because I'm not as worried that you comment on the contents of them, but I want you to tell me what they are, who they are to or from, so if you take each one and tell me -- let's take the first one, which is MFI111. First of all, does this look like an authentic document to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll pose an objection to that. Your Honour, this witness -- some of these documents, it's plain, are not -- are not necessarily documents that he may have seen. I make it clear, I don't object to this being done so that they can be, but a comment like -- a question like that one, doesn't appear to be authentic. It begs many a question of expertise. And if he's going to be asked as to authenticity, he better be asked whether he's seen it before first. Because it's now 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this question is superfulous.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no need to ask this question, especially to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I really meant is does it look like a document that he has seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could ask whether this witness has seen this document or not before.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before, Mr. Gusic, other than the time I was showing it to you during proofing?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you recognize this document?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the command of the 4th Corps and signed by Commander Pasalic, the late Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And who is this -- purportedly this order addressed to?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I can't see very well, but as far as I can see, it says: "IKM of the Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And it's from Commander Arif Pasalic, or that's what it purports to say.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Arif Pasalic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will be at some later stage proofing the -- the documents, but at this moment the witness is just commenting and I'm marking them for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The next one, Mr. Gusic, which is 112. Could you tell us who this is to and from purportedly.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document either because it was sent by General Pasalic, again to the IKM of the Supreme Command Staff in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The next one now, have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. I couldn't have seen this one either because, again, it's from the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to whom is it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: To the Jablanica IKM. And again, the commander is the late Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And the last document.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Again, it's addressed to the IKM of the Supreme Command Staff to General Halilovic personally. The commander is Arif Pasalic, the late Arif Pasalic. Again, it's from the 4th Corps, and I couldn't have seen this document either because it wasn't forwarded to me. And it shouldn't have been forwarded to me either.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Why shouldn't -- why should it not have been forwarded to you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the corps commanders were at the same level of command, so it wasn't their duty to provide personal documents to each other but only to the superior command. They could only provide documents for information if certain actions were taken in the vicinity of the zone of responsibility of the adjacent commander and then this would affect the life and work of the unit of the adjacent commander, as this was not the case in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And the last document.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a document from the 4th Corps command. It was signed by Tetak [phoen], uncle, the Chief of Staff of the 4th Corps. It's to the Supreme Command staff IKM, and General Halilovic and Zulfikar Alispago. Personally, again, I have not seen this document before, and it has nothing to do with me, but it probably relates to the other document that I was looking at a minute ago because, as far as I could see when I looked at it briefly, an OG North 2 was formed and its commander was the commander of the special purposes unit, Zulfikar, that is to say, Zulfikar Alispago, and that is probably why the Chief of Staff provided it to his unit and to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, you did have an opportunity to see these documents at -- and give them detailed consideration during proofing, did you not? You looked at them?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. During proofing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And you've read them.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I mean, Your Honour, I can wait for the witness to read them all here again, but would that be acceptable to the Defence that he's read the contents of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The Defence has no doubt that he's read the contents of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think there's no problem. But I wonder if it's the proper time for us to take a break at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll take a 20-minute break and then we'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please indicate how much time do you still need to finish the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to endeavour to complete it today, but I may run over 10, 15 minutes into the next session. But I'm going to endeavour to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, just before the break, I had shown you five documents. Now I'm going to show you another three. And these are 01853829, and that's MFI116 and 65 ter 45; the next one is 01853828, MFI117, 65 ter 46; the next one is 02131909, MFI118, 65 ter 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I forgot about the microphone. We'd object to this -- the one that's labeled number 53, 02131909, for that to be shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, would you please tell me what is the 65 ter number. The 65 ter number, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 53, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I thought I said that in the initial position. We'd object to that one being shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's on a different topic. It seems to be -- it's described as being an order from the IKM at Jablanica to the 4th Corps to send an individual, Mr. Alispahic, for a meeting. It's different from the reporting and the, if you like, the matters which this witness would be familiar with by way of internal protocols and so on like that. It's just a message. Now, again without pre-empting anything about witnesses, Mr. Alispahic is likely to be one of some controversy as well. So we object to documents relating to him. Unless the witness has seen this document himself, in which case we've got no basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any response?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no difference with this document from the others, but I will put it to the witness and ask him whether he's seen it before. Otherwise, I will -- I will show it through Mr. Alispahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, if the Defence team did not show any prejudice to their positions by showing this document, so we'll allow all documents to be used by the Prosecution team. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you look at the first document, Mr. Gusic. Like you did with the last ones, could you please tell us what this document purports to be.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is a document -- it's an explanation in the form of a report from the members of the Supreme Command Staff to General Halilovic, and it is about combatants that General Karavelic has to forward. And they're requesting a more detailed explanation. This has the form of a report, and there is also a request for consultations, and it also asks for information on the meeting held the previous evening. So this is a report sent by the members of the Supreme Command Staff and the IKM, and it's addressed to the commander of the Supreme Command; that is to say, to General Halilovic. It's interesting to see that it was forwarded from the Jablanica IKM and that it arrived in Sarajevo. It was received by the communications centre in Sarajevo, and that's all I could say about the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. And the next one? Who is it from?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The same individual signed it. It was forwarded to the same address. And this is a report, an explanation stating that they can't receive certain troops from General Karavelic. And they're informing General Halilovic that if they don't have a reserve force of 200 men, they won't be able to carry out the task that they had planned to carry out. They are requesting vehicles -- they're requesting that the vehicles went to fetch those soldiers return to Jablanica if they failed to secure the forces that were requested. So again, this is a kind of report and request. At the end of document, under paragraph 2, there is a request. The address is the same; it's from the Jablanica IKM. And its destination is in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And the third document, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order that doesn't contain all the elements of an order. But since the Minister of Internal Affairs at the time is concerned, I think that it's logical for it to be addressed to the corps command by General Halilovic because the communications between the 4th and the 6th Corps were not normal. So in order for this to arrive in Konjic -- in order to arrive in Konjic for a meeting with Mr. Rusmir Mahmutcehajic, it was necessary to keep this document confidential. That's why it says it's strictly confidential. But it doesn't contain the elements of a standard order; although, this could be an order. In fact, it is an order. It's an order that has been issued by General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, you have seen these series of documents, and I would like to ask you: What do you -- what is the gist of these documents?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the first series that I had a look at before the break, these documents related to the duties of the commander of the 4th Corps, with regard to the Jablanica IKM and General Halilovic, and these documents had the form of reports or orders to his subordinate units. Whereas, the second series of documents, the last three documents, have the form of reports or information from the IKM. And again, this is an order from General Halilovic to the late Arif Pasalic, General Arif Pasalic. So they're a series of documents consisting of reports and orders from the 4th Corps to the IKM and from the IKM to the 4th Corps, and there's also internal correspondence from the members of the Supreme Command Staff, or rather, from the members of the Jablanica IKM.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Now, I'd like to ask you where you were personally in September, starting from 6th to the 20th.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I think I was in the Konjic and Fojnica sector. Around the 20th, I was in the Fojnica sector, my IKM in Fojnica. That was around the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything about Grabovica during that period?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: At that period -- well, two or three or five days later from my assistant for security, Eminovic Nermin I received an oral report according to which a crime had been committed down there, and I was informed that he had sent a police company to the scene but the police company did not enter the scene since they said that there was ongoing combat action, that it was under control, and that this action would be organised by the Jablanica IKM, or those measures would be taken by the Jablanica IKM.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So who was -- you said Eminovic was your chief of security, is that correct, in your corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. He was my assistant for security. He was an assistant for all security matters in the corps. He was on a level with an assistant for intelligence or the assistant for morale, the assistant for logistics, the assistant for legal affairs. So as far as his professional work was concerned, he was on the same level as the Chief of Staff because the Chief of Staff was in charge of the operations in the staff. So these officers were directly responsible to me for carrying out certain tasks, certain professional tasks within the field of their duties, and Eminovic was one of those officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can you recall exactly what he told you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to remember all the details because a lot of time has passed since then. All I know is that at the time he told me that the units that had left Sarajevo had been involved in an incident, that people had been killed, that civilians had probably been killed. And he said that as soon as he received that information, he sent a police company from the 6th Corps police battalion to the scene. However, they weren't able to enter the area because the officer in charge of security affairs at the Jablanica IKM said that the time was not right because of combat operations, and he said that these measures would be taken and organised by the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Naturally, I have not been able to remember everything. I've just used my own words to tell you what happened. But I think Eminovic informed the security administration in the Supreme Command Staff in Sarajevo of this event. This was the procedure that should have been followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What did you understand by the Sarajevo units when you said -- what do you -- what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, these units were units that we had received a few days before and we helped them to get through to Jablanica. Parts of the 9th and 10th Brigades, parts of the Delta Brigade, and parts of a unit -- well, I can't remember the name of the command of the unit. The order stated that these men should be received and that we should help them to get through. So those are the men from these units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I would now like to show you a document, 04034725, MFI119, and 65 ter 166.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May we refer to Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, I understand that -- what you are going to say, Mr. Morrissey. And during the break, we have received a copy of this document, and we believe that there's no, as I said before, immediate danger of prejudice to the Defence team, and the contents of this document we also believe is relevant to this case, so we'll allow the Prosecution to use this document at this stage. But it does not mean that this document has been admitted into the evidence. At a later stage, the Defence team has the full right to challenge the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you look at this document, and would you tell us what it is, please, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is a report from the military police battalion commander to the 6th Corps and to my assistant for security, Nermin Eminovic. It concerns the events that took place on the 10th of September. It concerns action he took on the 10th of September in Jablanica and in order to control and assist in the work of the subordinate unit in Jablanica. This was a unit of the 44th Brigade. It's not very legible, but it has to do with the genocide over the Croatian population in Grabovica. So he's saying that he went to the scene and that Namik Dzankovic told him that nothing was being done with regard to the matter and that he had received this order from Mr. Vehbija Karic. I haven't seen this document before, and it wasn't necessary for me to see it because this is correspondence between -- or from the professional organs to my security organ, and it's probably on the basis of this information or similar information that Nermin Eminovic informed me of this event.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I will take you to the last paragraph of this particular document, where it says: "We went to Jablanica, where I carried out consultations with Namik Dzankovic from Sarajevo UVB Military Security Administration and he told me that the SVK, Supreme Command Staff IKM forward command post knew that and that it had been ordered not to do anything because of the planned operation." Could you explain what this means and were you told this by your security officer?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps this is what he said or perhaps he said it in the way that I put it earlier on. But it means that the commander of the military police battalion saw Namik Dzankovic from the military security administration. This is an administration department within the Supreme Command Staff in Sarajevo. And he was told since he was familiar with the problem, that the Supreme Command Staff IKM was familiar with the problem, and that an order had been issued not to do anything because of planned combat operations. He received this order from Mr. Vehbija Karic. The order not to do anything was received by Dzankovic from Vehbija Karic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And did this information -- did Mr. Eminovic give you this information that you alluded to earlier?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, not these details. I can't remember that he told me that Vehbija Karic had issued an order not to do anything, but he told me about the event. He said that the police had been down there to provide assistance and that that assistance had been refused. That's what he told me. As to who issued an order not to do anything -- well, he probably didn't tell me because that wasn't important for me, because Vehbija Karic was a member of the Jablanica IKM. He was directly under General Halilovic, and I couldn't order him to change anything and nor could his order in any way affect my decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: He may not have told you the specifics of names and details, but what the general report of it, was that communicated to you, as per this particular document and what you see? Whatever you see which has been said in this document, was that conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Again, that is -- that is a leading question that you can see from what went before is an attempt to repair the problems. The witness shouldn't be asked a leading question at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Chana, you should build the case step by step, one question after another.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's just that I thought the witness had said that these are -- this is the information he was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that. But you should do it smoothly, one peel after another.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'm guided by you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I'd like to go back to this conversation you had with your chief of security, Mr. Eminovic. Can you look at this document, please, and whatever it says. And can you please tell the Chamber from this information that you see what you were personally told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, excuse me. Could the witness stop for a moment. Once again, this is an attempt to force the witness's hand. The witness has said already what he can remember, and I have no objection to my friend asking him to think again and try to remember more. But to ask him whether he's prepared to adopt something from a thing that he's never seen is really, in my submission, impermissible. It's an attempt to get what has not successfully been got so far. Therefore, I don't object to my friend seeking the detail she wants by legitimate means, but not to put it into his mouth, so to speak. So that's the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't see your way, Mr. Morrissey, in this aspect. But, Ms. Chana, could you ask a simple question, a very simple question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What did Mr. Eminovic tell you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Nermin Eminovic, my assistant for security, transmitted to me the information relating to this report. I'm not sure he told me the number of people who were killed. I don't think he told me the manner in which they were killed. But he did tell me that a crime had been committed, that the units that had arrived from Sarajevo had participated in the crime, that a military police unit had attempted to go to the scene but had not succeeded in doing so. And as far as I can recall, that's what he told me. More or less. He told me that the problem there had occurred and that the forward command post knew of the event, that the IKM knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Now, I would like to ask you about the troops in the -- in that region at the time. Do you know of any subordination orders personally that were given to any troops?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I also had such orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I will show you now --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you give me a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's 01850315, MFI120, and 65 ter 35. May we refer to Sanction, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about this document.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order on organisational changes in the zone of responsibility of the 1st, 4th, and 6th Corps, and it's based on the decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Changes are ordered in the organic composition of the 3rd Corps, the 6th Corps, the sabotage and reconnaissance unit is entering the 6th Corps, the Crni Labudovi, or Black Swans, are reincorporated within the structure of the 6th Corps. The Zulfikar and Silver Fox units shall form part of the structure of the 4th Corps. The Muderiz Independent Unit. And then the order of the 4th of July of the staff of the Supreme Command is no longer in force. The commands of the 4th and 6th Corps are to take over the units referred to with respect to all elements of combat readiness, combat use, organisation, and so forth. The command of the 4th Corps is tasked with providing financial and logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you look at number 7, please, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Number 7: The officer at the IKM shall provide the necessary specialised assistance to the commands of the 4th and 6th Corps in executing the tasks set forth in this order. To this end, the commands of the 4th and 6th Corps shall establish the necessary contacts with officers at the forward command post, the staff of the Supreme Command of the BH Armed Forces."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic -- I'm sorry, Mr. Gusic. What was your understanding of this?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order to the officers, that is, to the IKM, to give assistance -- specialised assistance to the commands of the 4th and 6th Corps in establishing the new organisation pursuant to this order. This implies the transfer of one unit to the 2nd Corps and vice versa. If we connect this to paragraph 4 - and it is connected - they're to help in all the elements of combat readiness and combat use. They are to help these units to find their place in -- within the corps, to be given tasks, and in accordance with the new structure to carry out new planning, and based on these plans, to make use of these units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Who is to make use of these units?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: It follows from this order that these units were to be used by the corps commands and the specialised assistance in the use of these units in the initial stages. Until these units were brought fully into their establishment, they had to be given the necessary support. This order does not directly indicate any specific combat operations. It is aimed at preparing these units for their future use. It doesn't give any specific tasks to be carried out by those units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. I will now refer you to document 00 -- 02122414, and it's 51 on the 65 ter list, and it's MFI121. Can you tell us about this document, please.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order on resubordination, the resubordination of units in the combat disposition. The first part of the document: The preamble mentions the units, Zulfikar, Muderiz, Akrepi, and Silver Fox. And then tasks are given. These units, together with the Dreznica battalion, make up the OG North 2. This is a temporary formation set up to carry out a specific task. The commander of the OG is appointed. His name is Zulfikar -- he's the commander of the Zulfikar Unit. His name is Zulfikar Alispago. And this document is addressed to him. The area of responsibility is defined.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you look at item --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: And under 3, the task was supposed to be defined but the task will be defined by the forward command post of the Supreme Command Staff in Jablanica. This was not the usual way of proceeding because the -- whoever established this unit was supposed to give it its task. But this is evidently a question of resubordination, which is why no specific task is mentioned and room is left open for the IKM in Jablanica to assign a specific task. In point 4, the commander of the Zulfikar Unit is given the task of informing all commanders of the units with this order. This means that only Mr. Zulfikar Alispago received this order, and that's why this task is given. The other three commanders are to be informed of it. The command was issued by General Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Is there any connection between this document and the last one you just saw?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The connection is evident in the preamble. I haven't looked at the number, but I think they even refer to the number of the other document. Up to that time, these units had not been part of the 4th Corps. It was only by the previous document that you showed me that they became part of the 4th Corps. That's when they were deployed within the combat disposition of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you yourself have any authority in this particular area, your corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: How do you mean "authority"? Do you mean in carrying out combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Authority in respect of the command between you and -- the chain of command. What was your role, given that the IKM was there?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: We have just seen the rules of service and the superior-subordinate relationship, so I think that my answer is superfluous. But since you asked, I could not have any control over those units because there was a senior command and the senior officer directly on the ground in command of those forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document. There are two actually. I'll just read out both names. 02141683, MFI122, 65 ter number 47; and the other one is 01805262, 65 ter number 39, MFI123.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: May we refer to Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about this document.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is a combat order in which a task is assigned and resubordination is carried out of part of the units within the framework of, as it says here, the Zulfikar Reconnaissance and Sabotage Brigade, the Dreznica Battalion and units of the 1st Corps are mentioned here. These are probably the units I've mentioned before. Then the artillery weapons are enumerated, which are put at their disposal. Some brief information is provided as to the expected enemy response. The command of the 6th Corps is tasked with providing six field telephones. The commander of the Zulfikar Brigade is tasked with taking over the hydroelectric power plant on Neretva River, and he's tasked with regulating the level of the water because this will probably affect the future combat operations, and instructions are given as to the use of the distributed technical equipment and materiel. And this command was delivered to the Zulfikar Reconnaissance Sabotage Brigade, or rather, its commander, the 6th Corps commander, and the 4th Corps commander, as well as the archives, to General Halilovic personally and to the commander of the Dreznica Battalion. Colleagues from the communications centre are asked to forward this document from the 6th Corps to the 4th Corps in Mostar. This is a standard operative order, a combat order.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Can I now refer you to the next document. Could you please tell us the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 39, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is an order whereby the following units, the Handzar Divizija, the Silver Fox Unit, become part of the special purposes detachment Zulfikar. This order was written in connection with the decision of the Main Staff of the 21st of August in Zenica with a view to making larger units out of smaller ones. And this is an organisational order in form; although, personally I think that this kind of order should have been signed by the commander since it relates to organisation. We can also see it as an order on resubordination, although it doesn't state so explicitly. Rather, this unit is ordered to enter the organic composition. So it is an organisational order after all. It should contain certain elements about manpower levels, replenishment, and so on. Although it can be carried out in its current form, when it relates to the transfer of a unit from one composition to another. The other elements can be ordered later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Could you now please tell the Chamber whether anyone asked you, as a 6th Corps commander, for assistance in the matter and the incident which had happened in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. No. If you're asking about assistance, this can also be viewed as assistance. For example, the transfer of a unit from one unit to another in the form of an order. Such orders did arrive. But as to solving the problem in Grabovica, the specific problem in Grabovica - I'm referring to the crime that was committed - no one ever asked me for assistance about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did Mr. Eminovic tell you anything about whether he had been asked for assistance?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: No. No. But he could have had that through the command and control chain, from General Jasarevic. He could have received instructions. If he asked him not to inform me or anyone else, then he didn't do that, but he could have taken certain steps without informing us. This did not happen infrequently. Certain things required by the administration were ordered directly through the chain of command of the security organ while the chain of command did not know about it. They would know at the level at which the decision was reached. But I would not necessarily have to know about it or any of the lower-ranking commanders if such a decision was made. I can't say that this was always the practice, but it did occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you in a position to render assistance if asked in -- in such an investigation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, had he -- we could not have provided complete assistance only with army units, but if we had been asked for assistance, we could have assisted in cooperation with MUP units. We could have asked for assistance from the police stations in Jablanica, Konjic, and Fojnica, and they would certainly have provided us with assistance, as would have the Hadzici police, the Visoko police, and others. And directly we could have secured the scene. We could have activated the military police unit with the equipment it had at its disposal, which was modest, but all the same we could have provided some assistance. But I do have to say that I cannot guarantee that we would have been successful in performing our task. There was always a possibility that somebody would hinder the investigation, as these were units over whom I did not have direct command, nor was I able to control those units. But if I had put my units at the disposal of somebody else who could control them, then something might have been done. I think that directly -- had I directly carried out this task or, rather, my organs in my command, then the outcome would not have been certain. Because I could not command units which were not in my organic composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Now, I want to take you to now, again, back to mid-September 1993 and ask you whether you had any meetings with the accused, Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I think on several occasions. I can't tell you the exact number of meetings, but I'm sure that I was with him, General Bilajac and General [indiscernible] at the Jablanica forward command post. I can't recall the precise date. But this was when the IKM was being set up in early September. I met him in the first ten days of September on the road to Dugo Polje near Prozor in the village of Kruscica. On the way towards the village of Voljevac, I was coming from Konjic and he, I think, was coming from Jablanica - I don't know - or maybe even from Sarajevo. And there we had a brief meeting in the village of Kruscica. General Halilovic spoke to some local villagers. We took some refreshments and rested a little. And then we continued on our way to Dugo Polje -- or rather, we went to see the commander of the Independent Prozor Battalion. We held a meeting there. At that meeting, General Halilovic asked for me to be present. At that meeting, the possibility was considered of using the Prozor Battalion on the axis in the direction of Prozor jointly with the forces of the West OG under the command of Brigadier Selmo Cikotic, and we stayed there for quite a long time. We had a meeting with Commander Buza. What I can say about this meeting is that it was there that I heard about the decisions on the axis. The main one was along the Neretva; then this was changed and the main axis of attack was to be in the direction of Prozor. The battalion commander Buza then informed General Halilovic that he could not carry out the task in the way they had discussed previously. Buza was supposed to infiltrate his forces into the town of Prozor, and they were to begin operations from the rear. He then briefed the general that he was unable to do that. All the members of the staff of the Supreme Command who were present expressed their displeasure. Mr. Karic was there. I think General Zicro Suljevic was there and General Bilajac. General Halilovic expressed his displeasure. I cannot express his precise words. I have to paraphrase. But he said that the combat operations had been brought into question because of the change in the information as to the possibilities of the Prozor Battalion. And this meeting ended in quite an unpleasant atmosphere. No concrete specific tasks could be assigned to the Prozor Battalion, and then Cikotic accepted some obligations in connection with his axis. I think that the late Mr. Enver Zejnilagic, the commander of the 317th Brigade, which was a part of the 6th Corps, also accepted some assignments. We left in the afternoon, and I don't remember that after this I saw General Halilovic again. Maybe we met on the road again, but in this period I was usually at my forward command post in Fojnica. This was the other task we had been given at the meeting in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Tell me, how many directions of attack were in your area, the 6th Corps? How many directions of attack were you supposed to undertake for this operation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: At my forward command post, there were two directions of attack. This was a doctrinal approach. We always had to have a main direction of attack on which we placed the focus and an auxiliary direction, which was supposed to create the conditions for us to carry out our intentions on the main axis or in the main direction. Neither of -- well, each of these was established with realistic expectations, and we expected to succeed in both those directions of attack. As for the operations we planned in the Fojnica area, they were supposed to extend the connection with the forces of the 3rd Corps because in that area the HVO forces held the dominant features and they were cutting off our main communication connecting us with Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can I go back to the meeting when you said that Enver Buza and Mr. Halilovic was there at a meeting with yourself. What were -- exactly was the problem? What was the discontent about? Briefly, please, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, they were unhappy because when I arrived, everything had been planned and prepared. Commander Buza was supposed to introduce his battalion in the wider area of the town of Prozor. And when the sign was given to start combat operations, he was to go into combat with the -- against the HVO forces. He was to attack them from the rear. He was supposed to take the forces to the enemy rear and to carry out the attack against the HVO forces there. And this is a good decision to take when it's possible to proceed in this manner. But Buza said that the forces had been detected, he had been detected, and his reconnaissance had been spotted, and he said that no one would be able to get through to that axis or return alive. And the other members also expressed their discontent because of this situation. This is an unfortunate situation. If this happens before the combat operation, then the combat morale above the units is also put into question, and that probably put into question the execution of the entire task. I must say that when Buza accepted the first task, he thought it would be possible to carry out the task but he didn't have all the information he needed in order to assess whether he would be able to actually accomplish the mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Other than that, was there any other problems with continuing with the attack or launching this attack which was discussed at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the change of the focus point was a serious problem. Changing the focus of the attack was a problem. It was supposed to go from Neretva to Prozor. And doing that without introducing new forces, new equipment is not correct. You can't just say I'm going to change the main axis now in a decision. You can express the desire to have more success on the secondary axis, but you can't say that you're going to turn the secondary axis of attack into the main axis of attack. That's not sufficient. Certain things need to be done in order to make such a claim.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you remember what date this meeting was? Can you please try and see whether you can remember?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to remember, but I think it was between the 10th, 12th, or 13th -- the 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, or 13th of September. I can't remember the exact date. But I think you could find the exact date in Sevko Hodzic's book. There is a photograph, and I'm in the photograph. It's in Dugo Polje. I think he spoke about that meeting, so perhaps you could find the exact date there. But I think it was during that three-to-four day period.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if you tell us, was it before or after your meeting with Eminovic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I think it was before. I think it was before.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's fine. I want to show you now this document again, 02098431, 65 ter is 66, and MFI124.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could we refer to Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this document, please, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: This is the standard combat order in which brief information is provided on --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: -- the axis of operations. It was sent by the chief of the Main Staff, General Halilovic, and it appoints a commander for the axis from the 317th Brigade. It's a 6th Corps brigade. The subordination of certain units to the commander of tactical axis and the independent battalion Prozor, part of the 45th Brigade, part of Sutjeska Brigade. That's the brigade from the -- the battalion from the 81st Brigade. They are providing equipment, zone of responsibility, and a task is -- are issued. This is a standard order issued to the commander of the 317th, the 45th, and the Prozor Independent Battalion by -- it's issued by General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Now, I would like to ask you: Do you know whether this operation went ahead by the Prozor Independent Battalion under the command of Enver Buza?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The independent battalion participated in the combat operations on the axis that I have just mentioned. It was involved in combat operations on that axis, but the operation was not successfully completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you please explain what you mean, that it was not successfully completed.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't move any of the lines that they were supposed to move. They were supposed to take control of certain areas, establish new defence lines, and as far as I know, they didn't succeed in doing this. But they were involved in combat in that area, but they remained at the lines they had been at before the combat operation commenced.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What was the name of this area where this operation -- what was the name? Yes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: The area of the operation? Well, the area of that group of villages was called Uzdol, and the entire area is the Rama Lake area within the Prozor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you hear about anything which may or may not have happened during this operation? Did you get any information after the operation?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I had certain information I obtained through the media. The first -- or the initial information I received was through the public media. There was information according to which a crime had been committed in Uzdol by --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: -- army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. What date was this?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date. It was in the second half of September, but I don't know the exact date because -- because after the meeting that I have spoken about, after I'd gone to the IKM in Fojnica, we launched combat operations towards Kiseljak and Kresevo, but it was in any event in the second half of September. And according to information I got, the late Smiljko Sagolj, well, he was someone who knew that there were a lot of lies relayed by the media and the media --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Which -- which media did you hear this from?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, look, usually I was able to listen to the radio. I didn't have a television. So I heard it on the daily news. That was when I first obtained information according to which something of that kind had happened up there. But I didn't believe it because it wasn't the first time that the media relayed such information and the information was not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, can we just go a little slower. I just want to ask you a couple of questions. This radio programme, I still want to know, please, where was it broadcasted from?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, it was probably broadcast from -- well, I can't say exactly. I don't know where the transmitter was. But it was probably from territory that was under HVO control. But I listened to Sarajevo Radio too just so that I could get some information and so that I could know what was happening in various parts of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What did this radio programme inform you of? Briefly, Mr. Gusic. What exactly were you -- did you hear?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me to tell you a lot, since 13 years have passed since then, but on the whole it was that members of the ABiH had committed a crime against the civilian population and that they had killed -- well, I think they said about 20 people, women, children, the elderly, innocent people. They said that they had set light to part of the village and that they had withdrawn. On the whole, that was, roughly speaking, the information that I heard at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Where was this? Did they say where it was?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you hear about it from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, soon afterwards the commander asked for a report, General Delic. He asked for information on the event.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... but did -- was there any other person that you talked about this incident with?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. With Commander Buza. I contacted him and asked him about it, and I think that on that occasion he also sent a written report to the corps command, a report on that event. And if you want to know what the report stated exactly, well, all I could say is at the time he said that they were involved in combat operations, HVO forces had sustained losses. He mentioned some numbers that I can't remember right now. But what was interesting is that he said that there were extremists from the HVO in civilian clothes. Apparently they didn't have a sufficient number of uniforms. And one shepherd entered the zone of combat with his sheep and sheep were killed and he was killed. So that was more or less the information that was received, and we forwarded that information to General Delic in written form and orally as well. And perhaps that was around the -- because something else happened on the 20th, so it was on the 20th for sure. There was a problem with an American citizen in the territory of Vrda. She'd been detained by the forces from the 45th Brigade. Because at the time I was in Fojnica, and the late Izetbegovic contacted me personally and asked me to resolve the problem. And just after that - perhaps a day or two later - there was this event, and then we established contact via telephone and via radio, and I think that I then relayed information of that kind to General Delic, information on Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Under whose command was the Prozor Independent Battalion who launched this attack, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: In the combat operations, it was under the command of Commander Zejnilagic, and this was on the tactical axis, the commander of the 317th Brigade. It was under the IKM Supreme Command Staff headed by General Halilovic. But it was part of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, do you remember if there was ever a cease-fire declared in the area around that time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If I can show you this document which might assist you, 01859031. It's 70, 65 ter number; MFI125.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a supplement to the order, but there is an order that came before this one. And I think that the previous order was signed by General Siber.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: But the basic thing is the cease-fire, according to this document - and I'll take you to the middle of the first paragraph - "The Joint declarations, signed in Geneva on 14 September 1993 by President Alija Izetbegovic and Franjo Tudjman, President of the Republic of Croatia." Is that your understanding of -- of the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I want to move quickly along now. I can see the time is late, Mr. Gusic, because -- do you know whether combat actions continued after the -- this date? Of the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Combat action did continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honours, to that end, I've got the last three documents which I will show the witness. It is 0219 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Chana, it seems to me that we cannot finish the testimony of this witness, and I believe that we have to stop at 7.00, on time. So maybe we'll continue the direct examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I've endeavoured my hardest to finish by the appointed, but I am just left with a very small part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite understand. I appreciate very much your effort, but we have to stop at 7.00. It's too late.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day and you have to understand that you're under the oath. So during this period, please do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope you have a good rest today. And we'll resume tomorrow morning -- tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 4th day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
